insurer: Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Not specified in provided extract (Base Sum Insured + Booster+ + Safeguard/Safeguard+ + ReAssure+/ReAssureX as per Policy Schedule/variant)

great.name: Room Rent
great.quote: “We don’t limit your choice. Choose the room you like, but choose judiciously to protect your Sum Insured.”
great.explanation: No room category cap is stated, so you can choose any hospital room. This reduces the risk of room-rent restrictions cutting your claim payout.

great.name: PED Waiting Period
great.quote: “...Pre-existing Disease (PED) ... shall be excluded until the expiry of 12months/24 months/ 36 months (as per Variant selected) of continuous coverage...”
great.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 12/24/36 months depending on the variant selected. A 12-month option is faster than most retail plans and helps you get PED cover sooner.

great.name: Specific Illness Waiting
great.quote: “...listed conditions... shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months/12 months (as per Variant Selected) of continuous coverage...”
great.reference: Section 5.1.2 Specified disease/procedure waiting period (Code- Excl02)
great.explanation: Specified diseases/procedures are covered after 12 or 24 months depending on the variant selected. The 12-month option is better than the common 24-month waiting period.

great.name: Restore Benefit
great.quote: “ReAssure “Forever”: Enjoy unlimited Sum Insured. The first paid claim in the life of the policy triggers ReAssure “Forever”. Once Triggered it stays for life, provided that the policy is renewed without break.”
great.explanation: Unlimited restoration (“ReAssure Forever”) starts after the first paid claim and continues for life if you renew without a break. This can significantly increase available cover across future claims beyond the base Sum Insured.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of any Illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an Accident...”
good.explanation: Illnesses are not covered for the first 30 days from the policy start date, while accidents are covered immediately. This is a standard market waiting period.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: “...for 60 days before the date of admission...”
good.reference: Section 4.1.3 Expenses before and after hospitalization (Pre & Post hospitalization)
good.explanation: Medical expenses are covered for up to 60 days before hospitalization. This helps pay for tests and consultations leading up to admission.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.reference: Section 4.1.3 Expenses before and after hospitalization (Pre & Post hospitalization)
good.explanation: Medical expenses are covered for up to 180 days after discharge. This supports follow-up treatment and medicines during recovery.

good.name: Air Ambulance
good.quote: “Air Ambulance: Only in case of Emergency. We will pay up to Base Sum Insured.”
good.reference: Section 4.1.1 Expenses in reaching a Hospital
good.explanation: Emergency air ambulance is covered up to the Base Sum Insured. This can help in critical situations where rapid transfer is needed.

good.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.quote: “Home Care Treatment means treatment availed by the insured person at home... we will pay... provided that: a. The medical practitioner advices... b. ...continuous active line of treatment... c. Daily monitoring chart...”
good.explanation: Home treatment is covered when medically advised and supported by continuous active treatment and daily monitoring records. This is useful when hospitalization is not possible but treatment is still required.

good.name: Organ Donor Cover
good.quote: “...we will pay the hospitalization expenses of the donor for harvesting the organ, ONLY when your Hospitalization claim is paid.”
good.explanation: Donor hospitalization expenses for organ harvesting are paid only if your transplant hospitalization claim is paid. This reduces the financial burden of donor-related hospital costs during a covered transplant.

good.name: Worldwide Coverage
good.quote: “This Policy covers Allopathic treatments anywhere in the world.”
good.explanation: Allopathic treatments are covered worldwide. This can help if you need treatment outside India, subject to the policy’s claim and payment terms.

good.name: AYUSH Treatment
good.quote: “AYUSH treatments are covered in India only.”
good.explanation: AYUSH treatment is covered only within India. This provides alternative medicine coverage domestically but not for treatment taken abroad.

good.name: Modern Treatments
good.quote: “We pay for Modern treatments, up to Base Sum Insured for the list as specified below...”
good.explanation: Modern treatments are covered up to the Base Sum Insured for the specified list. Coverage is available, but only for listed procedures/technologies.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: “Annexure I - The expenses that are not covered... List I – Expenses not covered”
bad.explanation: Consumables are listed under expenses that are not covered. This can increase out-of-pocket costs for items like gloves, masks, and other hospital disposables.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: “Co-payment means a cost sharing requirement...” and separately “Optional Benefit: ... 4.1.16. Co-Payment...”
bad.explanation: An optional co-payment benefit is offered, which means you may have to bear a percentage of each claim if selected. Any applied co-pay increases your out-of-pocket share even on admissible claims.

unclear.name: No Claim Bonus
unclear.quote: No explicit NCB/cumulative bonus accrual rate and reset terms provided in the supplied extract (only definition of 'Cumulative Bonus' appears).
unclear.explanation: Only a definition of Cumulative Bonus is shown, but the accrual rate and reduction/reset rules are not provided in the extract. You cannot confirm how much extra Sum Insured (if any) builds up for claim-free years from this text alone.

unclear.name: Proportionate Deduction
unclear.quote: “If you opt for a Hospital room which is higher than the eligible room category as specified in your Policy Schedule, then We will pay only a pro-rated portion...”
unclear.explanation: A pro-rated payout applies if you take a room higher than the eligible category mentioned in the Policy Schedule. The impact depends on what room category your schedule makes you eligible for.

unclear.name: Cashless Network
unclear.quote: “Cashless claim facility is available at our network hospitals ONLY. As list of network hospitals is dynamic, for the latest list, refer to our website...”
unclear.explanation: Cashless treatment is available only at network hospitals, and the network list is maintained on the insurer’s website. The number of network hospitals is not stated here, so convenience cannot be judged from this extract.
